issues.body: build_join_index treats parent_cols.is_empty() as an unconditional cross product, and JoinIndex::lookup returns that entire parent-subject list for every child row. Under R2RML, join conditions may be omitted when the child and parent triples maps use the same logical table; the referencing object must then be the parent subject generated from that same current row, not every parent subject. For example, a self-reference over rows 1 and 2 should emit row1->row1 and row2->row2, but this code emits all four pairs. Omitting conditions for different logical tables should not silently acquire this non-standard meaning.
issues.fix_hint: Represent the omitted-condition same-logical-table case separately and evaluate the parent subject map on the current child row (or otherwise retain row correspondence). Reject a referencing object map with no join conditions when the logical tables differ. Replace r2rml_join_no_conditions_is_cross_product with a real-path same-table test that has at least two rows and asserts only row-correlated objects, plus a failure test for different tables without rr:joinCondition.
issues.title: Omitted join conditions incorrectly produce a cross product

verdict.summary: The graph-union correction from round 2 remains sound, but the referencing-object-map implementation still gives the wrong semantics to an omitted rr:joinCondition. R2RML permits omission when the child and parent triples maps have the same logical table; in that case the parent subject map is evaluated against the current child row. The implementation instead indexes every parent subject and emits a cross product, and it also accepts omission across different logical tables. This can silently generate spurious relationships. Because this is a newly identified major correctness issue after a clean prior round, progress is regressing.
